newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mostly up on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mostly up on liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Friday, with institutions liquidating many positions, traders said.

The key November 1996 contract ended at 3,302 yuan ($397) per tonne, up seven yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 3,282 and hit a high of 3,310. Open interest fell sharply to 53,900 lots from 79,480. One lot is five tonnes.
The January contract rose 11 to 3,237 yuan, March 19 to 3,254, May fell 25 to 3,285 and the first traded July and September ended at 3,300 and 3,348.
Combined volume rose sharply to 141,600 tonnes from 17,400.
Traders said institutions liquidated large positions due to uncertainty over the short-term market trend.
"Institutions wanted to move their money into more active markets due to a lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
Traders said investors will continue to offset their positions around 3,300 yuan in the next few days.
